Hi Sarah — thanks for the note and the clear questions. I pulled together a concise mapping below so your risk team can paste answers into the SIG. I also attached a small evidence bundle and a short matrix (see attachments).

Quick summary (high level):
- Hosted (Redwood API):
  - Control plane: Redwood-managed (US and EU control-plane endpoints, region chosen by customer during onboarding).
  - Data plane: customer request processing happens in our managed compute; customers can request region pinning for data residency (we support us-west/us-east/eu-west at GA).
  - Key management: service-managed keys by default; we offer Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) via KMS integrations for enterprise plans.
  - Multi-tenant isolation: logical tenant isolation with per-customer tenancy, strict namespace separation; not physical single-tenant GPUs.
  - Evidence to attach: redwood-hosted-arch-diagram.png, SOC2-Type2-2026.pdf (high-level controls), hosted-data-residency-policy.pdf.

- Dedicated (Reserved capacity):
  - Control plane: Redwood-managed control plane; customer has dedicated GPU pools for inference (single-tenant at the compute level).
  - Data plane: inference occurs on capacity reserved for the customer (no co-mingling of customer workloads on those GPUs).
  - Regions: dedicated pools can be provisioned in specific regions; for enterprise contracts we can commit to region residency in the SOW.
  - Key management: BYOK supported; KMS integration for disk and model artifacts.
  - Evidence to attach: redwood-dedicated-dataflow.png, dedicated-tenant-isolation-statement.pdf, security-ops-runbook.pdf.

- Private (VPC / On-Prem):
  - Control plane: optionally customer-hosted control plane (private control plane) or Redwood-managed control plane with private network peering.
  - Data plane: deployed inside customer VPC or on-prem cluster; customer retains network control and can enforce outbound rules.
  - Key management: customer-managed keys (HSM/KMS) standard; no service-managed keys unless explicitly enabled.
  - Audit & evidence: audit logs live in customer account/collector; we provide configuration guides and a signed attestation for audit log delivery.
  - Evidence to attach: private-vpc-deployment-guide.pdf, kms-integration-checklist.docx, data-flow-onprem.png.

SIG-specific guidance for answers: map controls to the following buckets we used in the questionnaire: Data Residency & Locality, Tenant Isolation, Key Management, Audit & Logging, Network Controls, Service Access Controls. For each answer, reference the matching artifact from the attachments. For example: Q-3.2 (data residency) -> attached hosted-data-residency-policy.pdf; Q-5.1 (tenant isolation) -> dedicated-tenant-isolation-statement.pdf.

Next steps:
- I can compile a single zip with the artifacts above and a short cover note that lists which SIG question each artifact supports.
- Aditya (copied) will pull the SOC 2 Type II extract and the latest network diagram. Marissa from Security will join if you want an architect-level call.

Would you prefer the evidence bundle as a Drive link or an attached zip? I can do either.

Best,

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Hi Sarah — Marissa from Redwood Security here. Quick answers to the two points so you can annotate the SIG: 

1) Dedicated: model artifacts for dedicated pools are stored on customer-dedicated volumes. We do not store other customers' model artifacts on those volumes. The evidence file "redwood-dedicated-dataflow.png" highlights the isolated storage paths and the SOW language we use for dedicated capacity.

2) Hosted: our telemetry/observability pipeline collects anonymized operational metrics; we do not send raw request payloads or PII to third-party analytics vendors. Any monitoring that requires logs containing PII is ingested into our internal audit pipeline and routed to customer-controlled storage when requested (see "hosted-data-residency-policy.pdf").

I'll attach the data-flow diagram and a short callout doc that references SIG question IDs. If you'd like a 30-min technical call to confirm, I'm available Wed-Fri this week.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
